subject: BrightCo MSA - customer content & model training language
messages:
From: Matthew Dunn <matthew.dunn@brightco.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>; procurement@brightco.com
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@brightco.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightCo MSA - first-pass redlines (customer content & training)

Jasmine — thanks for the call this morning. As discussed, attached is BrightCo's first-pass redline of the MSA and order form focused on two areas we flagged: (1) output ownership and attribution for customer prompts + model outputs, and (2) training/use of customer content for model improvement.

High level asks from our side: 
- BrightCo needs clarity that any customer-provided prompts and unredacted outputs will not be used to train or improve vendor models without explicit consent.
- We propose a feedback license narrowly scoped to telemetry needed for service quality (anonymized usage metrics only).
- If Redwood intends to retain rights to outputs for product development, BrightCo requests a carve-out where customer-provided data cannot be used for model retraining without a separate agreement.

Attached: BrightCo_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (redlines) and a short spreadsheet summarizing the redline locations. Please confirm receipt and let us know the earliest your legal/dev ops can review.

Cheers,
Matthew Dunn
Head of Procurement — BrightCo

Jasmine/Laura — quick technical notes after reviewing BrightCo_MSA_redlines_v3: 
- We can implement an opt-out that prevents any customer-provided content from entering retraining pipelines. Operationally that's a config toggle tied to the customer's tenant; it adds overhead to retention policies and increases storage/compute costs because we cannot leverage aggregated signals across tenants.
- For telemetry-only license (anonymized request/latency/error metrics), that's low-cost and already part of our monitoring pipeline; no PII or prompt/response content would be included.
- If BrightCo requires a contractual ban on using outputs to improve models across Redwood, we'd have to maintain a segmentation boundary and typically recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment (which supports guaranteed isolation).

Estimated uplift for a no-retrain guarantee on hosted plan: +20-35% list depending on retention/audit SLAs. For Dedicated/private we'll scope separately. Happy to sync and draft the ops impact section for legal.

— Karthik
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 14:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightCo MSA - first-pass redlines (customer content & training)

Team — thanks, useful summary. A few legal framing points and suggested contract language below. I’ve highlighted compromise positions we can offer immediately and items that require escalation to Sales Leadership / Pricing: 

1) Narrow feedback license (recommended): 
- "Customer hereby grants Vendor a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated, de-identified usage metrics and telemetry solely to monitor, maintain, and improve the Service; such telemetry shall not include raw prompt text, unredacted outputs, or customer-identifying metadata."

2) No-retrain carve-out option (commercial): 
- Offer an explicit clause: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data, including prompts or outputs that contain Customer Data, to train or improve Vendor models used for third parties, except pursuant to a separately negotiated agreement." 
- Make this contingent on either: (a) Dedicated/Private deployment, or (b) a managed-hosted plan with a contractual surcharge and operational audit rights.

3) Short-term negotiation strategy: 
- Respond within 48 hours acknowledging receipt. Offer (i) our standard telemetry-only language as baseline, and (ii) a written path to a no-retrain carve-out (with pricing and deployment options) to be finalized in an addendum. 

4) Attachments: I prepared a short redline snippet that swaps BrightCo’s proposed absolute ban for conditional language that preserves our product improvement rights while giving them contractual certainty. Let me know if you want me to send the proposed snippet to BrightCo directly or route it through you, Jasmine.

I’ll draft the suggested snippet and an internal memo explaining legal risks if they insist on a full ban. Markus — flagging for pricing uplift approval if we go commercial.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_snippet_no_retrain_carveout.docx (DOCX)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCo MSA - first-pass redlines (customer content & training)

Matthew — thanks for sending these over and for the clear summary. We’ve reviewed internally and can outline two paths as a starting point: 

1) Standard telemetry approach (fast path): We can accept a narrow feedback license limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry (latency, error rates, feature usage) that excludes raw prompt/response text and customer-identifying metadata. This requires no change to architecture and we can commit to language within 48 hours.

2) No-retrain carve-out (commercial path): We can contractually agree not to use Customer Data for retraining Vendor models used for third parties, but this will be scoped either to a Dedicated deployment or a hosted plan with a commercial uplift and audit provisions. Our legal and engineering teams have drafted conditional language and a pricing uplift estimate; if BrightCo wants to pursue this, we’d propose an addendum and a short commercial discussion.

Laura and Karthik are on the thread to provide the suggested snippet and ops impacts. Would you prefer we (A) send our proposed revisions to the MSA redlines directly, or (B) set a 30-minute call to walk through the two paths? Please let us know availability this week.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
